app.title: Western Blot Quantifier: multi-threshold band detection
app.summary: A person uploads a western blot image. The tool finds the horizontal rows of bands, and the person picks which row to analyse. They can set a merge threshold, then press Analyse. The tool finds every band in that row without being told how many lanes there are, draws a box around each band with its number, and marks it as strong or weak. It then shows the row's horizontal signal profile, bar charts of each band's volume and its intensity relative to the largest band, and a table the person can download as CSV.

task.text: Detect the bands in one row of a blot image, measure each band's background-subtracted volume, and export each lane's intensity as a percentage of the strongest band.

data.text: A single greyscale or colour image of a gel or membrane with dark bands in lanes, reduced to a table of per-band measurements.
data.item: a band in one lane of a blot image

stage.text: measuring band intensities from a blot image after imaging, before comparing conditions

mechanism.text: The uploaded image is shown next to a copy with the detected bands boxed and numbered, with count badges below. The chosen row and the merge threshold control the detection. Below, a profile plot, two bar charts and a table all number the bands the same way as the overlay, and the table can be downloaded as CSV.

field.text: western blot densitometry in molecular biology

workflow.name: detect objects in an image and measure each one relative to the largest

steps.here: Drag a PNG, JPG or TIFF blot image onto the uploader. It is shown at full width with its size and the number of band rows found.

steps.step: choose the region to work on
steps.here: Peaks in the vertical profile give the band rows. When there is more than one, a dropdown chooses which row to analyse.
A merge-threshold slider sets how narrow a band can be, relative to the median width, before it is merged with its neighbour. A checkbox turns the profile plot on or off.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: Analyse runs multi-threshold erosion to find band centres. It clusters them into lanes, merges bands that are too narrow, fits each box to its profile, and sums the background-subtracted signal as the volume.

steps.step: check the result against the source
steps.here: Numbered boxes are drawn on the image, green for strong bands and yellow for weak ones, with counts in badges. The horizontal profile shows each band's span and peak.
Bar charts show each lane's volume and its relative intensity as a percentage of the largest volume, with a 100% reference line.
A table of lane, position, size, volume, mean intensity, type and relative % is downloaded as quantification_results.csv.

distinctive: The number of lanes is never entered: lane positions come from clustering band centres found at many threshold levels.
Bands that are too narrow compared with the median width are merged repeatedly, and one slider controls this.
Each lane's intensity is reported relative to the strongest band, not as an absolute amount.
Each band is classed as strong or weak by its peak intensity, and the class is shown by box colour and in the table.
